To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exercise-induced ST-segments elevation was significantly greater in patients with homozonal than in patients without ischemia and that exercise-induced ST segments elevation was significantly greater with remote ischemia than with no ischemia.
the presence of ischemic area adjacent to infarcted area enhances exercise-induced ST-segments elevation in the territory of infarcted artery.
the degree of exercise-induced ST elevation is higher when myocardial ischemia occurs in the same vascular territory as the infarction than in other vascular territories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of myocardial infarct size on exercise-induced ST segment elevation and exercise capacity one month after myocardical infarction.
the study of the effect of the myocardial ischemia adjacent on the ST-segment elevation induced by the myocardial exercise.
the effects of myocardial ischemic adjacent to infarct on ST-segment elevation in the early post-infarction period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the exercise test is a very useful tool for the diagnosis of myocardial ischemic disease, and the ST segment changes are a good indicator of the presence or absence of ischemia in patients with acute myocardial infarct.
the presence of ischemia adjacent to myocardial infarct enhances the magnitude of ST-segment deviation in the infarct zone during exercise.
myocardial ischemia adjacent and distant to infarction can amplify exercise-induced ST-segments elevation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
myocardial ischemia adjacent infarction enhances exercise-induced ST-segement elevation one month after acute myocardial infarct.
myocardial ischemia adjacent or remote to the infarct zone enhances the magnitude of ST-segment depression or elevation during exercise.
exercise-induced ST segment elevation is a sensitive indicator for myocardial ischemia adjacent infarction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise-induced ST-segments elevation can be a useful non-invasive method to detect myocardial ischemia adjacent the infarction.
exercise-induced ST-segement elevation can be a sign of ischemia, but not necessarily of ischemia in the same area as the infarct.
the presence of remote ischemia does not enhance the magnitude of exercise ST elevation.
